about: The phrase check that must hold before the AI may ask for a transfer with the reason caller_asked. It looks at the last three CALLER turns (never the AI's): a turn counts when it does not carry a role marker or tell the receptionist what to say, and at least one of its sentences matches a rule and no block. The OAIY host runs it on recentCallerTurns when it plans the ring, and the Aokie plugin runs the same rules first, so a model that claims caller_asked after a caller who asked for nothing of the kind is refused with caller_did_not_ask before anything is asked of the host. Both implementations are tested against this file, and the plugin's floor is meant never to be stricter than the host's own check: it is the host's check without names and without what only the host reads (an ask taken back, being told to say it, a different target such as billing, someone else in the room), with the difference about acknowledgements that the backchannel block states, and with one difference of writing: the host also removes the invisible joiners and marks (hex 200C to 200F, 2060, FEFF) that the normaliser here turns into a space, which matters only for typed text. Rules are the reference implementation of the design's appendix A.9, widened with the forms OAIY counts.
algorithm: 1. Take the caller's turns oldest first, leave out the ones that only acknowledge the AI (see backchannel), and keep the last recentTurns. 2. Cut each to its last turnChars characters (Unicode scalar values). 3. A turn asks when all of these hold: (a) roleMarker, matched case-insensitively against the turn as it was said, does not match; (b) the turn's plain text is not empty and no pattern of turnBlocks matches it; (c) at least one sentence of the turn is matched by at least one of rules and by none of blocks. The plain text of a text is normalise applied to it, then split at single spaces, without the words in fillers, joined by single spaces. The sentences of a turn are the pieces of the turn as it was said between characters in sentenceEnds, each made plain, the empty ones dropped. 4. The check passes when at least one turn asks. In every pattern <person> stands for person and <head> for head. The cases of window are turns already without the acknowledgement-only ones (steps 2 to 4 only); the cases of backchannel run step 1 too.
normalise: Lower-case; every character in removedCharacters (the soft hyphen, hex 00AD) is removed outright, not made a space, so a word with one inside it reads as the word; the apostrophe look-alikes U+2018, U+2019, U+02BC, U+201B, U+2032, U+FF07, U+0060 and U+00B4 become the ASCII apostrophe; every run of characters outside [a-z0-9' ] becomes one space; every run of spaces becomes one space; trim. So "speak, to the owner" normalises to "speak to the owner" and matches, and a caller's curly apostrophe ("I don’t want to speak") is blocked exactly as the straight one is. In JavaScript: s.toLowerCase().replace(/\u00ad/g, "").replace(/[\u2018\u2019\u02bc\u201b\u2032\uff07`\u00b4]/g, "'").replace(/[^a-z0-9' ]+/g, ' ').replace(/ +/g, ' ').trim().

names: The rules have no names in them. A caller who asks for the owner by first name is recognised only by a host that knows the owner's name (OAIY takes it from a business named for its owner: "Dave's Lawn Care" gives "dave"); the plugin has no owner name, so its floor does not count such a request and answers caller_did_not_ask, and the caller is offered a message instead. Cases with names are OAIY's own and are not part of this file.

backchannel.about: Turns that only acknowledge the AI ("mm-hmm", "yeah, okay") are not turns to the plugin: it drops them from the caller's history before it takes the last three (a request must not be pushed out of the window by the caller's "yeah"), for the phrase check and for the recentCallerTurns it sends the host. The OAIY host leaves an acknowledgement out of its own record only when it was said over the AI while the AI was talking (and leaves out a turn said before the greeting, one that resumed a reply that was cut off, and a quick "of course" or "go on" said over the AI); an acknowledgement said in a pause after the AI had finished is a turn in its record. The plugin cannot see any of that audio timing, so it decides by the words alone. The cases of window and of positive and negative above are already turns without them; the cases below give the turns as the call carries them, the turns that remain, and whether the check passes. The difference runs the allowed way, because the plugin's check is a floor under the host's and an acknowledgement-only turn can never be what asks: dropping more of them only lets the last three reach further back. The one way the plugin can be stricter is a turn the host drops for its timing that the plugin keeps, which uses one of the plugin's three places.
backchannel.rule: Lower-case the turn; split it at whitespace and at hyphens (U+002D, U+2010, U+2011 and U+2013); in each piece keep only its letters and digits and drop the pieces that end up empty; read the words left to right, where a word that with the next word forms one of pairs is one acknowledgement (both words used), otherwise a word in words is one acknowledgement, and anything else means the turn is not an acknowledgement. A turn is a backchannel when it is at least one and at most atMost acknowledgements.

knownGaps.about: Kept so nobody mistakes this check for more than a floor under the host's own policy (initiative setting, limits, quiet hours). A case the check gets wrong on purpose would be listed here; changing one means changing this file on both sides. None are known: the three that used to be listed (a request that is itself negated, and something said about someone else) are refused by the blocks now and are ordinary negative cases.
